The transparent cornea forms the curved front surface that refracts incoming light rays into the eye. Behind the cornea lies the aqueous humor filling the anterior chamber, followed by the iris controlling pupil diameter, and the crystalline lens which focuses light onto the retina. The vitreous humor fills the large posterior chamber providing structural support. The optic nerve emerges from the back of the eye as a thick bundle of nerve fibers transmitting visual signals from retinal photoreceptors directly to the brain's visual cortex. The choroid layer beneath the retina supplies oxygen and nutrients through its rich vascular network. The sclera forms the tough white outer fibrous layer providing structural integrity.
